evidence.title: June 2026: From Tokenized to Composable, Making Onchain Assets Actually Work

new_value.evidence_detail: Falcon reported USDf supply of $1.26B and total reserves of $1.3B, a 103.32% backing ratio, on 1 July 2026. The same public update identifies BTC (64%), mBTC (14.5%), and enzoBTC (14.2%) as the leading reserve exposures. Applying the rubric's 50% top-three-asset shock to that 92.7% reserve share leaves approximately $697M of reserves against $1.26B USDf supply (about 55% backing), well below 110%. This calculation concerns USDf only; Anchorage-issued fUSD is a distinct product and is excluded.
new_value.evidence_summary: Falcon's 1 July 2026 USDf update reported 103.32% backing and 92.7% of reserves in BTC, mBTC, and enzoBTC. A 50% shock to those three reported exposures leaves backing far below the 110% stress threshold.

old_value.evidence_detail: The qualitative control description cannot substitute for the factor's required reproducible stress result.
old_value.evidence_summary: Falcon describes dynamically calibrated non-stable collateral ratios, but no reproducible stress simulation or asset-level inputs establish whether net collateralization remains above 110% under the rubric scenario.
old_value.notes: The public OCR documentation was reviewed for stress inputs and results; it explains calibration criteria and a buffer formula but does not publish the simulation needed to adjudicate the 110% threshold.
